town.text: Three roads meet here. South to the Low Ford, east to the Old Road and the Verge, and north... north is shut, and a boy in shiny armour will tell you why at length. Vonnra takes the toll, Holloway keeps the peace, Brannoc keeps the steel, Chid keeps the shrine, badly. Harlan and Pell keep each other honest. Mostly. And Sella keeps the blue room upstairs, and my third of it, and her mouth shut when it matters.

fortune.text: Sit. Give me your hand. No, the other one: the one you hold the blade with. No charge, this once. I have been waiting to see how it came out.

text.text: I see water running clear. Wolves in the deep wood where they belong, and a hole in the hillside with no poison coming out of it. You went looking for the cause and not the culprit. Most people never learn the difference.
I see wolves running beside you, not at you. The old grey one lets you walk in front. Holloway sleeps with his sword across his knees now. Be careful what you have taught them to follow.
I see pelts. A great many pelts, and a grey one on top of the pile. The road is safe and the wood is quiet. Something that was sick got sicker, and then there was nothing left of it to be sick.
I see a quiet wood. Too quiet. You made the road safe the way a fire makes a house warm.
I see wolves at the east gate, and a man of the Watch who did not come home. You were busy. The world was not.

I see clean water, and a ledger with a new line in it. The wolves are saved and Pell Varrow owns a hole in the ground. You were paid; he was paid. Someone always is. Wenna has not forgiven you, and she is the one who notices.
The wolves, I see only dimly. Whatever you meant to do about them, you have not done it yet.
I see a boy asleep in a wagon, and his uncle sitting up beside him all night. Salt and iron back where they belong. The Coyle Company will say your name at every table it sits at.
I see a boy come home, and a strongbox go the other way. Harlan will learn where it went. People always do.
I see three teamsters walking home, thinner than when they left. What became of the rest of it is between you and the Kerchiefs.
I see cages. I will not tell you what is in them. You know.
The caravan: a cold trail, cold cages. It is not finished. Neither are you.
And Pell. Pell in irons, being walked to the cells, telling everyone who will listen that he has friends. He does. They are not in this town.
And a ledger, with your name in it, in Pell's small tidy hand. You were paid. So was everyone else in that book. I would keep an eye on all of them.
And an empty warehouse, and a man on a fast horse who will not stop until he is somewhere that has never heard of the Coyle Company. He will not forget you.
And Pell Varrow, counting. He is always counting. One day he will count you.
And you. You have already died on this road. Most people only get to do that the once. Something did not want you to stay down, and I would very much like to know what.
And you. The Watch has your description. It is not flattering.
And you, who smell of the Pack now. Dogs in the square will not bark at you. People will.
And you. You came up the Low Ford road at night, and the lamps lit for you. They have not done that for anyone in a long time.

night.text: She takes the coins first and your hand second, and leads you up Rook's narrow stairs. The blue room smells of lavender and lamp oil, and the bath is, as promised, mostly warm. What follows is nobody's business but yours: slow, and warm, and unhurried, and for a few hours the road and the dead on it are a long way off. You wake with her hair across you and the sun already up. She is dressed, and counting.

what.text: Down there. Under the one that is dead. There is another. There is always another. Take the map, take it, I do not want to know where the tunnels go any more.

first.text: You are the one who opened the cage. I — thank you. Uncle Harlan has not stopped crying. It was not wolves, you know. A clerk at the gate said the road was shut, and sent us down the forest track, and they were waiting.

You have the look of someone who walks toward trouble on purpose. Good. I am Ysolde Marrow, and I draw maps of the places the road forgets: woods that eat their own paths, barrows that open after dark, ravines the Kerchiefs think are theirs. Each one sworn under oaths. Each one ruled by something that will not want you there.

choices.text: What will I find out there?

text.text: Back from the edges, {name}, and in one piece. The places you took are quieter for it. I have new ones.
Maps, {name}. Places the road forgets. Pick one.

choices.text: What will I find out there?

oaths.text: Every map is sworn under something, written in the margin. The Long Winter, and their blows chill you to a crawl. The Blight, and nothing mends right. Iron, and only a clean critical cuts them. An oath asks something of you and pays for it in ember or in gear. Read what answers it: a cloak lined for the cold, a slayer's edge for the Pack. And what you find out there leans toward what the place wants of you. Run the Winter long enough and you will be dressed for it.

places.text: Sixteen clearings, give or take, strung along a way that doubles back on itself. The packs sleep where they stand until you are close, then wake together. Three altars in every map: wake one and hold its clearing while it calls, and it pays out when it is spent. And at the heart of the last clearing, whatever rules the place. Kill it and the map is yours, and the way home opens where it fell.

drawn.text: People like you. They walk in, and some of them walk out, and I buy what they remember before the drink takes it. The ones who do not walk out, I draw from where their light went out. You can see it from the road, if you know how to look.
